title: How a handle creates
claim: How a handle creates. Glue two census knot spaces along one simple 3-edge cut and remove a line on the near side (768 removals: every ordered pair, lines 0 and 1 spliced into point 0). (1) Every new knot at the opened cut (936 of them) has three points: one in the removed line's tie class (the hub), one near point off the ports, one far point. (2) Two elementary lemmas. An assignment u of near points and v of far points occurs iff the port patterns allowed by u and by v meet, since the solutions are a join along the ports. A derivation never grows, so a three-point knot is generated iff two generated three-point knots inside one of its four-point extensions produce it; at all 768 removals, eliminations among three-point knots alone generate the same three-point knots. (3) For every new knot {h, a, c}, h and a pin the ports to one pattern t (its complement when both flip), and each value of c excludes one of t and its complement: a joint use of all three ports that no single port carries. (4) This is necessary but not sufficient: new knots occur only at six-pattern removals where some pair pinned by the hub and a near point is separated by a far point (100 removals), 100 such removals create nothing, and no four-pattern removal creates (512). (5) On the Fano plane every removed line meets the closing line in one port, the hub is tied to that port, and every pinned pair's odd port is that port (96 removals, 52 creating); census 58 creates both this way and with the removed line missing the closing line and the hub tied to no port.
failure_conditions: A new knot at a single opened cut with more than three points, or not through the removed line's hub.
A new knot whose hub and near point do not pin a complementary pair that its far point separates.
A removal with new knots and no pinned pair separated by a far point.
A Fano removed side whose six-pattern removal has the hub off the closing line or a pinned odd port elsewhere.
foundation_claim_scope: Knot spaces glued along one simple 3-edge cut from two census spaces; eliminations up to ties.
